findings.title: Brownfield guide fixture is under-specified; Tasks 9T, 10T and 12 can't verify "concept prompt" or "Phase 2 prompt"
findings.description:
Task 9T (lines 194–195) builds the `brownfield-guide` fixture by adding "a `brownfield-adoption: [...]` profile line" and a `##### Brownfield Adoption` section to the test-project prompt file. That file has no `context_profiles:` block and only these sections: Context Initialization, Tool Usage, implementation, design, review and Task Breakdown.
- `ContextProfileParser.parseProfiles` (`ContextProfileParser.ts:131-146`) needs a `context_profiles:\n` key inside a code fence. A lone profile line parses to `{}`, so every selected build would hit the "no profile" `AdoptionError`.
- The fixture has no Concept or Architecture prompt. For `Phase 0: Concept`, `getPromptForInstruction` returns null and `SectionBuilder.buildInstructionSection` (`SectionBuilder.ts:109-117`) falls back to "Custom instruction: …". Task 12 expectations 1, 2, 5, 7 and 9 say "concept prompt", and expectation 10 says "Phase 2 prompt". Neither is distinguishable from the brownfield prompt unless the fixture gains marked `##### Concept` and `##### Architecture` sections.
- Task 9T should say to add a fenced `context_profiles:` block and distinguishable Concept and Architecture prompt sections.

findings.title: History `reason` carries gitExec's network/VPN hint and a multi-line message
findings.description:
Task 5 (line 118) sets `reason` to the error message and says the timeout message "already reads 'timed out after 5s'". But `gitExec` wraps every error as `git <args> failed in <cwd>: <detail>`. `withNetworkErrorHint` (matching `/timed out after \d+s/`) then appends "This looks like a network/DNS problem reaching the remote. Check your VPN/proxy… guide.source…". For a local `rev-list`, that advice is wrong. The multi-line text also lands in a one-line Adoption Facts bullet (Task 8) and reaches the agent.
- Task 5T's assertion ("reason contains `timed out`") would pass anyway.
- Task 5 should say to derive a short reason: take the detail after `failed in <cwd>:`, drop the hint, and keep it to a single line. For example, "git timed out after 5s", as the design (D5) gives it.

findings.title: Resolver writes `in_progress` before gathering facts that can still throw
findings.description:
Task 9 orders step 5 (write `in_progress`, lines 188) before step 6 (`readHistory`, `presentPaths`, `recognizeCi`, render, line 189). `presentPaths` and `recognizeCi` throw plain `Error`s on non-ENOENT failures. Task 4T asserts the `ENOTDIR` throw, and `pathPresent` throws on broken symlinks.
- A plain `Error` is not rethrown by `generateContextFromProject`. It becomes the error stub, but the state is already `in_progress`.
- The next build then shows no "set by this build" notice, because `stateSetByBuild` is false. The project is committed to the brownfield prompt, and the user was never told or shown the facts.
- The design's own goal ("a missing profile never leaves the state written") argues for the same rule here. Reorder Task 9 to gather and render inputs first, then write, then set the notice flag. A write failure still throws before any prompt is produced.
- Task 9T should add a case where a fact gather fails and the state stays `''`.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkbox tasks
findings.description: Lines 78, 105, 131, 148, 178, 202, 225, 251, 257 and 269 are `- [ ] **Task NC: Commit**` checkbox items. The convention is a plain `**Commit**:` line, never a checkbox. As written, they count as tasks and can be left unchecked. Their placement is sound: each follows a green implementation and test pair. Convert them to plain `**Commit**:` lines.

findings.title: Task 13 parity test will not produce identical strings as specified, and its guide source is unspecified
findings.description:
Task 13 (line 248) builds "identical copies" in two temp dirs and asserts identical prompt strings.
- `recognizeCi` returns absolute paths (the design says "CI's absolute paths"). If the fixture contains any CI file, the two directories give different strings. Tell the task to use a fixture with no CI file, or to normalize the directory prefix.
- The MCP `integration-project` fixture has no brownfield profile. The existing permissiveness integration test copies fragments cross-package from core's fixtures (`mcpIntegration.test.ts:295-309`). Task 13 should name the same approach for the `brownfield-guide` fixture.
- `generateContext` (`contextTools.ts:90`) runs `ensureGuideForProject` on the temp checkout, so the fixture's guide must satisfy `GuideManager.ensureCheckout`. The permissiveness test shows this works with a copied fixture.
- The "CLI path" here is `createContextPipeline` plus the integrator, not `build.ts`. That is acceptable, but Task 13 should say so.

findings.title: "`context_build` returns the missing-profile error" has no test
findings.description: A success criterion (slice line 333) says the `AdoptionError` is returned as an error by `context_build`. Task 12 #12 stops at the pipeline rejecting. Task 11 only asserts which `adoptionStateWrites` value is passed. Walkthrough step 4 is CLI only. Add one `context_build` case with the profile-less guide that asserts `isError` and the `cf guides update` text. This fits beside Task 13 and uses the existing `build()` helper style.

findings.title: Task 10 guard should key on `checkoutPath`
findings.description: Task 10 (line 206) gates the resolver call on "the resolver and `project.projectPath`". After the move, `checkoutPath` is typed `string | undefined`, so passing it to the resolver fails to compile. The three existing resolvers guard on `checkoutPath`; do the same.

findings.title: No load or timing test; the stated reasoning holds
findings.description: The slice's sub-second target (D2) is bounded by cap tests. The task file explains why there is no `tests/load/` task: `tests/load/` is a Python rule, and no such directory exists in this repo. I verified both claims. No action needed.

findings.title: `detection/` imports policy from `adoption/`
findings.description: Task 3 has `sourceVolume.ts` import `BROWNFIELD_MIN_SOURCE_LINES` and `AdoptionError` from `adoption/`, while the design says `detection/` is "facts only, no policy". The design requires the walk to stop at the threshold, so this is acceptable. Both are leaf imports (`adoptionOutcome.ts` takes `SourceVolume` as `import type` only, `contracts.ts` has no imports), so there is no runtime cycle.

findings.title: Claims about existing code and caller updates are accurate
findings.description:
- `createContextPipeline` callers: Task 11's grep and the `build.test.ts:227` `toHaveBeenCalledWith('/tmp/test')` pin match the code. The callers are `build.ts:84`, `contextTools.ts:92`, `build.integration.test.ts` (four calls), `pipeline-integration.test.ts:57` and `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts` (six calls).
- `contextTools.test.ts:27` mocks the pipeline. `worktree-overlay.test.ts:32` mocks it but asserts nothing on its arguments.
- `node.ts:58` does `export * from './detection/index.js'`, and `index.ts:27` does `export * from './schema/projectSchema.js'`. `CONCEPT_PHASE` is therefore exported automatically, and the Task 4 barrel rule holds.
- The `gitExec(args, cwd, { timeoutMs })` signature matches Task 5.
- `ConfigManager.set` enum validation accepts `''`. The `ConfigManager.test.ts:440` key-count test is dynamic and unaffected by the new key.
- `resolveInitiativePlanPath` swallows every `readdir` error (`ArtifactIntrospector.ts:24-29`), as Task 6 states.
- The ordering sequences otherwise recover: the guide check precedes the write, and an explicit `--it brownfield-adoption` skips detection and the write. `ContextIntegrator.ts` is 377 lines as claimed.
